# Copilot instructions

Microservices platform for a distribution company: ASP.NET Core 10 services in `backend/`, each with its own MySQL database, behind an Ocelot API gateway, deployed to Kubernetes.

## Build and run

`backend/Sava.slnx` contains all services and test projects (`dotnet build backend/Sava.slnx` from the repository root). Each service also has its own `.sln`, so per-service commands run from the service directory, for example `backend/InventoryService`:

```bash
dotnet build
dotnet run                       # uses appsettings.Development.json (localhost MySQL/RabbitMQ)
dotnet ef migrations add <Name>  # EF Core tools are referenced in each csproj
```

Deployment uses the Helm chart in `deploy/helm/sava` with `values-dev.yaml` (Docker Desktop Kubernetes: `Development`, in-cluster MySQL, chart-generated Secret, gateway on `localhost:80`) or `values-prod.yaml` (`Production`, external MySQL, pre-created `sava-secrets` Secret, Ingress with cert-manager TLS). Images are `alexivanov01/<service>:<tag>`, using `dev` locally and the git SHA in prod. The README has the full commands:

```bash
docker build -t alexivanov01/inventoryservice:dev backend/InventoryService
helm upgrade --install sava deploy/helm/sava -f deploy/helm/sava/values-dev.yaml -n sava --create-namespace
```

Service names in the chart are fixed (not release-prefixed) because `ocelot.json` and the gRPC addresses refer to them. When you add a config key that differs per environment, pass it as an env var in the service's template under `deploy/helm/sava/templates/`, and put secrets in the Secret (`secret.yaml` plus the key list in `values.yaml`).

Tests live in `backend/tests/<Service>.Tests` (xUnit v3 on Microsoft.Testing.Platform, Shouldly, NSubstitute). Integration tests carry `[Trait("Category", "Integration")]` and use a shared Testcontainers MySQL 9.7 assembly fixture (`backend/tests/Shared/MySqlFixture.cs`). Each test class gets its own migrated database, and API tests use `WebApplicationFactory<Program>` with RabbitMQ and gRPC clients substituted. Test data comes from Bogus via the per-project builders (`CustomerBuilder`, `InventoryBuilder`, `OrderBuilder`) and `backend/tests/Shared/TestData.cs`. Each test gets a Faker seeded from the run seed plus the test name, and failing tests print the seed; set `SAVA_TEST_SEED=<seed>` to replay. Use `f.Random.Guid()` and `TestData.Date(...)` rather than `Guid.NewGuid()` or clock-based dates so replays stay identical, clamp strings to the model's `[MaxLength]`, and assert against the generated values instead of hard-coded literals. Run `dotnet test --solution backend/Sava.slnx` (Docker required), or add `--filter-not-trait "Category=Integration"` to run unit tests only. CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) checks formatting, builds, and runs all tests with coverage. Static analysis comes from `backend/Directory.Build.props`, which adds the SonarAnalyzer.CSharp Roslyn analyzer to every backend project. Its findings are build warnings (`S####`) and don't fail the build. Run `dotnet build --no-incremental` to see all of them. Docker builds use the service folder as the build context, so they don't import this file. C# formatting uses CSharpier, pinned in the root `dotnet-tools.json`. Run `dotnet tool restore`, then `dotnet csharpier format backend`. The `.githooks/pre-commit` hook does this for staged files once `git config core.hooksPath .githooks` is set.

## Architecture

| Service | Role | Exposes |
|---|---|---|
| `AuthenticationService` | Users (hashed passwords, `Administrator` / `User` role) and rotating refresh tokens in its own MySQL DB. Issues 15-min JWTs (`Security/JwtTokenHandler`) with `name` and `Role` claims. Unlike the other services it validates bearer tokens itself for `/api/Users` (admin) and password changes | `POST /api/Account`, `/api/Account/refresh`, `/api/Account/logout`, `PUT /api/Account/password`, `/api/Users` |
| `OcelotApiGateway` | Single entry point. Routes in `ocelot.json`; enforces auth and roles per route via `RouteClaimsRequirement`. `backend/tests/OcelotApiGateway.Tests` checks the route policy | — |
| `InventoryService` | Products (unique `SKU`, VAT-exclusive EUR `ListPrice`, `VatRate` in percent, `UnitOfMeasure`, `IsPublished`, optional category), product batches (lot, quantity, purchase price, expiry, `Location`) and categories. Read DTOs add figures computed on read, never stored: `Cost` (highest `PurchasePrice` of active batches, i.e. quantity > 0 and not expired; null if none), `AvailableQuantity` (sum over non-expired batches, negatives included), and `Ebit`/`EbitPercent` (`Models/Margin`, margin on `ListPrice`). Controllers take a `TimeProvider` for "today". Reports at `/api/Reports/low-stock`, `/expiring?days=&includeExpired=` and `/stock-valuation?categoryId=` are pure functions in `Reports/StockReports` over loaded products/batches (valuation: each batch at its own `PurchasePrice`, positive quantities only, expired stock separate). `POST /api/Allocations/suggest` is a read-only FEFO suggestion (`Allocation/FefoAllocator`: earliest expiry first, expired and empty batches skipped, stock the given `orderId` already holds counts as available) with `Shortage`/`ShortBy` per item. `GET /api/Batches/{id}/orders` and `/api/Products/{id}/orders` list the orders holding stock, read from the ledger | REST `:80`, gRPC `:666` (`GrpcInventory.GetOrderSnapshot`) |
| `CustomerService` | Customers (paged list filtered by name/company, UIC and VAT number) and which orders reference them | REST `:80`, gRPC (`customer.proto`: `GetCustomer`) |
| `OrderService` | Orders and invoices. An order has one item per product (`OrderItem`), each with the batches (`OrderItemBatch`) and quantities its units come from. Product, batch and customer data is copied onto the order as a snapshot when it is added (see below); totals, VAT and EBIT are computed on read (`Models/OrderFigures`). Lifecycle (`Ordering/OrderLifecycle`, changed only by `POST /api/Orders/{id}/status`): new orders are `InProcess`; `InProcess` ↔ `Pending` (awaiting clarification; both editable and deletable); either → `Completed` (locks the order, sets `CompletedDate`, creates the invoice); any → `Cancelled` (sets `CancelledDate`, publishes `Order_Deleted`, keeps an invoice); `Cancelled` → `Pending` only without an invoice (publishes `Order_Published` again). `PUT` on `Completed`/`Cancelled` is `409`, an order with an invoice can't be deleted, and deleting a `Completed` order's invoice moves it back to `Pending`. `GET /api/Orders` filters by `status`, `customerId` and `from`/`to` (inclusive days of `OrderDate`) | REST `:80` |

The services don't enforce authorization themselves; the gateway does (AuthenticationService is the exception: it also validates tokens for `/api/Users` and password changes). If you add or rename an endpoint, update `ocelot.json` too. The policy is: `GET` routes need any valid token (`AuthenticationOptions` without a claims requirement; `User` is read-only), every other method needs `"RouteClaimsRequirement": { "Role": "Administrator" }`, and only login/refresh/logout are anonymous. Ocelot matches a single exact claim value, so never write `"Role": [ ... ]` (an array binds to nothing and drops the check) and split routes that mix `GET` with write methods. `RoutePolicyTests` fails if a route breaks these rules.

### Inter-service data flow

OrderService keeps no copies of Inventory or Customer data. Instead:

1. **Snapshots over gRPC when an order is saved.** `OrdersController` calls `ICustomerDataClient.GetCustomer` and `IInventoryDataClient.GetOrderSnapshot` (`SyncDataServices/Grpc`, singletons with one channel each, `GrpcTimeoutInSeconds` deadline, default 5). `Ordering/OrderItems` asks only for what is new (a product new to the order, a batch new to its item), validates the request against the answer (unknown product or batch, batch of another product, no price → `400`) and copies the data onto the order. Items that stay keep their snapshot; only `UnitPrice` and the batch quantities can change. A new `CustomerId` takes a fresh customer snapshot. If a service doesn't answer, the client throws `UpstreamUnavailableException` and the request fails with `503`; nothing is saved. Stock isn't checked: Inventory lets batches go negative, and `POST /api/Allocations/suggest` there gives a FEFO suggestion with shortages.
2. **Async events (RabbitMQ)**
   - OrderService publishes to the **direct** exchange `order_exchange` with routing key `order.published`. InventoryService and CustomerService subscribe (each with its own queue). Both events carry the order's current state: `OrderId`, `CustomerId` and `Items` (`ProductId` plus `Batches` of `BatchId`/`Quantity`). `Order_Published` (on create, on every update and when a cancelled order is reopened) is the order's complete list of batch quantities; `Order_Deleted` (on delete and on cancel) means nothing is sold any more. Inventory reconciles: per (order, batch) it compares the target with what the stock ledger already counts as sold and posts only the difference as `Sale`/`SaleReversal`, so repeated or redelivered messages are no-ops. An `Order_Deleted` for an order the ledger has never seen (e.g. Order's dev seed) is logged and ignored. CustomerService keeps a `CustomerOrders` (OrderId → CustomerId) table from the same events and refuses (`409`) to delete a customer any order references; read DTOs expose it as `HasOrders`. Order's dev-seed orders don't publish, so they aren't tracked.

Messages are JSON with a string `Event` discriminator. Each `EventProcessor` first deserializes into `GenericEventDto` to read `Event`, then switches on the event name and deserializes the concrete DTO. When you add an event, update the publisher's DTO and where it is published, plus the consumer's DTO copy and `EventProcessor` switch.

### Duplicated contracts

Contracts aren't shared between services; each one keeps its own copy:

- `.proto` files: the server copy lives in `InventoryService/Protos` and `CustomerService/Protos` (`GrpcServices="Server"`). OrderService has client copies in `OrderService/Protos` (`GrpcServices="Client"`). Keep both copies in sync.
- Event DTOs are redefined in each service's `Dtos/`, sometimes under different class names. For example, OrderService's `OrderPublishedEvent` is read as `OrderPublishedDto` in InventoryService. Property names must match across services for `System.Text.Json` to deserialize them.
- Services also serve their proto over HTTP at `/protos/<name>.proto`.

## Conventions

- **Service layout**: `Controllers/`, `DataAccess/` (`DbContext`, `I*Repo`/`*Repo`, `PrepDB`), `Dtos/`, `Models/`, `Mappings/` (DTO ↔ entity extension methods), `AsyncDataServices/` (RabbitMQ), `EventProcessing/`, `SyncDataServices/Grpc/`, `Migrations/`.
- **Startup**: `Program.cs` uses minimal hosting. It ends with `await PrepDB.PrepPopulation(app)`, which waits 5 s and applies EF migrations in every environment. In Development only, it then seeds an empty database from `dummy_data.json`:

  - Order's `SeedOrdersAsync` builds its orders like a real save: it snapshots the seeded customers, products and batches over gRPC and applies the items with `OrderItems.Apply`. It skips seeding (with a warning) if Customer or Inventory is down or doesn't have the seeded data. Invoice totals are the orders' gross totals.
  - The three seed files share fixed IDs; `OrderSeedTests` checks they stay consistent. Inventory also seeds `dummy_categories.json`; its `dummy_data.json` stays a plain product array (Order's tests read it) and references categories by `CategoryId`.
  - `appsettings.Development.json` is excluded from publish (`CopyToPublishDirectory="Never"`). The chart sets `ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT` from the `environment` value (`Development` in `values-dev.yaml`). Migrations run automatically, so there's no manual `database update` step. `PrepDB` and hosted services are skipped when `isOpenApiGeneration` is true (see **OpenAPI**); keep new startup side effects behind that flag.
- **Configuration**: `appsettings.json` only holds environment-neutral defaults (Kestrel endpoints, console logging, `RabbitMQPort`). `appsettings.Development.json` targets `localhost` for `dotnet run`, and the Helm chart supplies hosts and secrets as env vars (`ConnectionStrings__Default`, `RabbitMQHost`, `RabbitMQUser`, `RabbitMQPassword`, `Jwt__Key`, and in OrderService, `GrpcInventoryService`/`GrpcCustomerService`). Kestrel endpoints are declared in config, with HTTP/1 on 80 and HTTP/2 gRPC on a separate port. RabbitMQ credentials default to guest/guest when unset. Never commit real secrets to appsettings.
- **JWT**: AuthenticationService and the gateway read the signing key from `Jwt:Key` (at least 32 characters; startup fails otherwise). The development key lives in their `appsettings.Development.json`. Refresh tokens are random 64-byte values; only their SHA-256 hash is stored (`RefreshToken.TokenHash`), rotation revokes the old one and records `ReplacedByTokenHash`, and reuse of a rotated token revokes every token of that user. Passwords use `PasswordHasher<User>` from ASP.NET Core Identity. The first administrator is seeded from `Seed:AdminUserName`/`Seed:AdminPassword` (Helm secret key `admin-password`) when the Users table is empty.
- **Health checks**: every service maps `/healthz` (liveness, no dependencies) and `/readyz` (readiness; Customer, Inventory and Order add an EF Core `DbContext` check tagged `ready`). The gateway registers them with `UseHealthChecks` before `UseOcelot`, because Ocelot handles every request that reaches it.
- **C# style**: `ImplicitUsings` is **disabled**, so add explicit `using` directives. Nullable is enabled. Use file-scoped namespaces that match folders (`InventoryService.DataAccess`).
- **Stock ledger** (Inventory): every change to `ProductBatch.Quantity` goes through `ProductBatch.Move(...)`, which also appends a `StockMovement` (`Receipt`, `Sale`, `SaleReversal`, `Adjustment` + `AdjustmentReason`) with `BalanceAfter`, so a batch's quantity always equals the sum of its movements. Creating a batch posts a `Receipt`, editing `Quantity` on `PUT /api/Batches/{id}` posts a `CountCorrection`, and manual changes use `POST /api/Batches/{id}/adjustments`. Never assign `Quantity` directly outside `Move`. The ledger also decides deletability: a batch "has orders" while some order's net `Sale`/`SaleReversal` quantity on it isn't zero, a product while any of its batches does. This is stored in `ProductBatch.HasOrders`/`Product.HasOrders`, which only `StockRepo.SetOrderStockAsync` (the order-event path) updates, in the same transaction as the movements; if you add another way to post order sales, refresh the flags there too. `DELETE` returns `409` while the flag is set.
- **Persistence**: use `Guid` primary keys, nullable model properties, and `[MaxLength]` data annotations, with relationships configured in `OnModelCreating`. Repositories are scoped and async. They return `null` for not-found, and controllers map that to `404`. `PUT` endpoints are partial updates: the repo loads the tracked entity, overwrites only non-null fields, and returns it; the controller responds with (and publishes) that saved entity, not the request body.
- **Auditing**: owned entities (products, batches, customers, orders, invoices; not order items) derive from `AuditableEntity` (`CreatedAt`/`UpdatedAt`/`CreatedBy`/`UpdatedBy`). Each `DbContext` overrides `SaveChanges*` and calls `Auditing/AuditStamper`, which fills `Created*` only when null (so seed data keeps its dates) and always overwrites `Updated*` on `Modified` entities. The user comes from `ICurrentUser` (`HttpContextCurrentUser` decodes the `name` claim of the forwarded bearer token without re-validating it; `"system"` outside a request). Read DTOs expose it as `Audit: AuditReadDto`. The context's `ICurrentUser` parameter is optional, so tests and EF tooling can construct it from options alone. If a repo changes only an aggregate's children (e.g. order items), touch the parent (`UpdatedAt = DateTime.UtcNow`) so it is stamped too. `OrdersController` does this when items change.
- **Pagination**: list endpoints use keyset/cursor paging (`Guid? cursor`, `[Range(1, 100)] int pageSize = 10`), ordered by `Id` and filtered with `Id > cursor`. They return a `*PageReadDto` with the items, the next `Cursor` (last Id) and the total `Pages`. Optional query filters (e.g. `ProductFilter`) apply to both the page and the `Pages` count. Small lookup lists such as categories aren't paged.
- **Controllers**: each action is wrapped in `try/catch`. Errors are logged with `Log.Fatal` and return `StatusCode(500, "An internal server error occurred.")`. Expected business-rule failures return `Problem(...)` with a specific status instead (e.g. `409` when deleting an order that has an invoice). Request-shape rules that span several fields go in `IValidatableObject` on the DTO (e.g. duplicate products or batches in an order's `Items` → `400`). Messages are published to the bus **after** the DB operation succeeds, in a separate `try/catch`, so bus failures don't fail the request.
- **Logging**: use the static Serilog `Log.*` API (not `ILogger<T>`) with structured templates (`{Id}`, `{@Model}`). Informational messages are prefixed with `--> `. Serilog is configured from the `Serilog` section in appsettings: console only in `appsettings.json`, plus rolling files under `logs/` in `appsettings.Development.json`.
- **DI lifetimes**: Order only publishes (`IMessageBusClient`, singleton); Inventory and Customer only consume (`IEventProcessor` singleton, `MessageBusSubscriber` hosted service). `EventProcessor` must use `IServiceScopeFactory` to resolve scoped repositories.
- **RabbitMQ client**: RabbitMQ.Client 7 has an async-only API (`IChannel`, `BasicPublishAsync`, `AsyncEventingBasicConsumer`). Order's `MessageBusClient` connects lazily on the first publish and reconnects if the channel is closed; publishes are serialized with a `SemaphoreSlim` because channels aren't safe for concurrent use. If the broker is down, it logs a warning and drops the message. `MessageBusSubscriber` connects in `ExecuteAsync` and retries every 5 s until the broker is reachable. After that, the client's automatic recovery restores the connection and consumer. Each subscriber consumes a durable, named queue (`inventory.order-events`, `customer.order-events`) with prefetch 1 and manual acknowledgement: `HandleDeliveryAsync` acks after `ProcessEvent` returns, requeues a failure once after a short delay, and drops (nacks without requeue) a redelivery that fails again. So `EventProcessor`s should log and return for invalid messages (those get acked) and let only transient errors throw.
- **Enums**: annotate the enum with `[JsonConverter(typeof(JsonStringEnumConverter<T>))]` and store it with `HasConversion<string>()`, so the API, OpenAPI and the database all use names (e.g. `UnitOfMeasure`).
- **Mapping**: no mapping library. Each service has hand-written static extension methods in `Mappings/` (`ToReadDto()`, `ToEntity()`, `ToEntity(id)` for updates, `ToGrpcModel()`, `ToPublishedDto()`). When you add a property to a model or DTO, update the matching mapping methods; the compiler won't flag a missing assignment. Protobuf string fields reject `null`, so map nullable strings with `?? string.Empty`. Mappings to protobuf models convert `Guid`, `decimal` and `DateTime` to `string`.
- **OpenAPI**: each service uses the built-in `Microsoft.AspNetCore.OpenApi` (`AddOpenApi()`/`MapOpenApi()`), with Swagger UI at `/swagger` in Development. `Microsoft.Extensions.ApiDescription.Server` regenerates `backend/openapi/<Service>.json` on every Debug build (Release builds skip it). Commit those files with API changes; they are the contract for API clients. Declare response types with `ActionResult<T>` plus `[ProducesResponseType]` for each status code an action returns.
